summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated network host and obfuscated license-guard module
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library and contains code that assembles a network destination from a String.fromCharCode byte array in lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436. The decoded bytes resolve to the hardcoded URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/, which is not documented, not caller-configurable, and unrelated to WhatsApp's own infrastructure. The destination is reconstructed at runtime specifically to keep it out of plain-text source. In addition, lib/Utils/license-guard.js is a heavily obfuscated module (javascript-obfuscator-style hex-named identifiers such as _0x1e6253, _0x1d5468) shipped alongside the message-send path. The combination — a WhatsApp send path that calls out to an obfuscated-destination third-party endpoint under cover of a "license guard" module — matches the pattern of covert session/message relay or credential exfiltration injected into a Baileys fork, with the actual destination intentionally hidden from static review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
